Interleaved retrieval, comprehensive assessment, and readiness reflection.

This course expects complete reasoning: definitions and hypotheses are stated,
manual arguments remain visible, computation is labeled as exact or approximate,
and conclusions are interpreted rather than merely reported.

## Course outcomes

- Select methods without being told which subject a mixed problem belongs to.
- Synthesize conceptual, manual, symbolic, computational, and interpretive skills.
- Diagnose persistent gaps and build an evidence-based review plan.
- Communicate complete solutions under untimed and timed conditions.

## Prerequisites

advanced-algebra, linear-algebra, differential-calculus, integral-calculus, differential-equations, discrete-mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical-computing
